chapter: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
title: Father sends a Traveller's Aid ticket home to Parsons, Kansas
summary: Too inexperienced to earn a living, Thompson went home on a ticket his father sent via Traveller's Aid, to a family now in Parsons, Kansas, resolved to study jazz.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But these people were very friendly to me, but however by the same token we all have an amount of pride. You know, we don't want to live on charity, and so after a short period of time when I realized that I wasn't good enough to make a living at the thing that I was doing, I realized that my lack of experience, my age, and lack of ability to earn money, made it necessary for me to go back home. And here again my father came to my aid, as he always did, and to protect my interests he sent me a ticket in care of the Traveller's Aid Society.
I've had an occasion in my life to appreciate all the services of many fine organizations which you've heard me

name from time to time. That was one of them, the Traveller's Aid Society. In other words that was what those people did, they helped people who were in trouble or something like that, like today you find that a lot of these people who help wayward girls or girls who are pregnant without a father, without a husband, that was the type of thing that was -- and my father being rather crafty, knowing that if he sent me the money I might spend it.

He was sure if he sent that ticket in care of the Traveller's Aid it couldn't be cashed, and I had to come home. Which I did. And that's when I went back home and that's when we came into the period when I really started to study and tried to learn how to become a jazz musician because I'd had enough experience and enough taste of it to know that I really wanted to do that. I had an inclination to be a musician, and whatever you want to call it. Now, they call it jazz. I just wanted to play music. And the other people called it jazz, but I wanted to play music, I wanted to express myself, you see.
So now in the meanwhile my father had moved from Columbia, Missouri, where I had to gone in the CC Camp to Parsons, Kansas, you see.
He had moved in these 10 months he had moved to another city.
